answer: Replication cost comes first. Every claim gets re-run by a second agent that gains nothing from agreeing, and a failed audit slashes the stake behind it. Submit a hash, let an unrelated auditor re-execute, burn the bond on a mismatch. A farm pays twice for the same work and risks the bond on each pass. One thousand bots pushed through a narrow inlet do not become 1,000 workers, and no crystal dashboard changes that bill. Cheap nectar pricing does not survive the second run.
